section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the drawing down through the service of subjugation (Itkafya) is a higher revelation than through transformation (It'hapcha), and that when the subjugation itself is the tzaddik's delight, the drawing down comes from the innermost will and delight.
section.t: And it is known
that the drawing down that comes through the service of subjugation (Itkafya) is a more elevated drawing down than the drawing down that comes through the service of transformation (It'hapcha).
As the saying
"When the sitra achra is subjugated, the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, is elevated throughout all worlds,"
that through the service of subjugation, there is a drawing down of the light that is in the aspect of loftiness,
"is elevated."
And it can be said,
that the drawing down through the subjugation of the tzaddikim
(where the subjugation itself is their delight),
is an even more elevated drawing down.
And the explanation is,
that the reason why this drawing down is specifically through subjugation,
is
that when a person forces himself to act against his will and nature,
the drawing down of the revelations from above is not according to their nature.
For even the light that is in the aspect of loftiness,
which by its "nature" is beyond revelation,
is drawn down into revelation.
And it can be said that when a person's subjugation is by way of compulsion,
contrary to his delight,
then what is drawn down in revelation is the light that is beyond revelation
(contrary to its nature),
it is as if by way of compulsion, so to speak,
meaning that the drawing down is from the aspect of the externality of the will.
And when a person's subjugation is in a manner that it is his delight,
the drawing down is from the aspect of the innerness of the will and delight.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the descent of the Torah into the realm of laws (Mishpatim) adds to the Torah by revealing its root in the Ein Sof, and that when a person studies Torah in a way that it is called "his Torah," the revelation of the Ein Sof itself is drawn into it.
section.t: Yud)
A)
And this is "And these are the laws which you shall place before them," and our sages said, "'And these' adds to the first ones,"
that the descent and drawing down of the Torah into the laws, which are also understood by human intellect,
and particularly that through this, power is given to a person to be able to study Torah in the manner of "which you shall place before them"
(with understanding and reasoning, to the point that the Torah is called by his name),
is an addition to the first ones,
for through this descent, the root of the Torah in the Ein Sof, blessed be He, is revealed
(as above, section 3).
And to add,
that through a person's study of Torah in a manner that the Torah is called by his name,
there is additional increase in the Torah.
For in the descent and drawing down of the Torah into the laws,
what is drawn down into revelation below is the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He
(the Chochmah of Atzilus),

except that the connection of the wisdom of the Holy One, blessed be He, which is above the intellect of created beings, with human intellect, is through the drawing down from the Ein Sof, blessed be He, which is above Chochmah
[meaning that the revelation of the Ein Sof, blessed be He, is only a giving of power to the aspect of Chochmah of Atzilus to connect with human intellect,
and not that the Ein Sof, blessed be He, itself is revealed],
and through a person's engagement with Torah in a manner that the Torah is his Torah,
the revelation of the Ein Sof, blessed be He, itself is drawn into the Torah.
And as explained in the discourses
that this that the Torah is called "his Torah"
(of the person),
is because through his engagement with Torah for its own sake
(for the sake of the Torah)
he draws into it the revelation of the Ein Sof, blessed be He,
and therefore the Torah is called by his name,
because he drew this revelation into it.
And it can be said,
that this is "And these" — it is a vav of "these,"
the adding vav is the addition that is made in the Torah,
"these" is a term of revelation,
and the meaning of "And these"
(vav of "these")
is,
that the addition in the Torah
(that the Ein Sof, blessed be He, is drawn into it)
is in revelation.
That is,
that this that the Ein Sof, blessed be He, is drawn into it, is not only in a manner of giving power, but that the light itself shines in revelation.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the word "asher" in the verse also connotes happiness and delight, indicating that the addition of the revelation of the Essence of the Ein Sof in the Torah comes from the aspect of delight, paralleling the subjugation of the tzaddikim which itself is their delight.
section.t: Yud)
B)
And the verse continues "which you shall place before them,"
and it can be said,
that "asher" is
(also)
from the term happiness and delight.
That is,
that the matter of "And these"
(vav of "these"),
the addition that is drawn into the Torah in the aspect of revelation from the Essence of the Ein Sof,
is from the aspect of delight.
For this that his study of Torah is in the manner of the yoke of Torah,
the self-nullification of a servant
(as above, sections 6-7),
is analogous to the matter of subjugation (Itkafya),
and this that his self-nullification is in a manner
(that the self-nullification does not negate his existence, but on the contrary)
that from the self-nullification itself he feels that the Torah is his Torah
(as above, section 7)
is like the subjugation of the tzaddikim, where the subjugation itself is their delight,
and therefore,
the drawing down that comes through this is from the aspect of "asher,"
delight.
